thread.title: Apple, Small Caps Up; Can Square Build More Gains? | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Apple, Small Caps Up; Can Square Build More Gains? | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The Nasdaq composite reasserted its leadership status amid mixed fortunes in stocks today . Apple continued to whittle away last week's 2.7% drop. Square, another true stock market leader, rushed to a new all-time high of 95.38 with less than an hour to go in the regular session.
X At 3:30 p.m. ET, the tech, retail and consumer-driven composite index rallied nearly 0.3% in otherwise quiet action by the key indexes. Leading stocks, however, continued to advance. The Innovator IBD 50 ETF ( FFTY ) advanced 1.4% to 38.04, boosting its year-to-date gain to 14.6%.
The S&P 500, down less than 0.1%, is up 9.1% since Jan. 1. Electronics contract manufacturing, semiconductor, container, chip equipment, paint, meat, cement and electric utility firms all dropped 1% or more as interest rates rose. The yield on the benchmark U.S. Treasury 10-year note hit 3.10%, the highest level since this year's peak of 3.11% set on May 17.
The Federal Reserve opened a two-day meeting on monetary policy and is widely expected to push the fed funds rate up another quarter point to a 2%-2.25% target range. This would be the U.S. central bank's eighth rate hike since December 2015.
Small Caps Outperform The Dow Jones industrial average kept losses small at less than 0.2%. It saw at least five of its 30 components lose 1 point or more, including insurer UnitedHealth ( UNH ), medical products titan Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ), insurer Travelers ( TRV ) and 3M ( MMM ).
Small caps outperformed. The Russell 2000 and the S&P SmallCap 600 both rose nearly 0.3%. The Dow Jones transports fell 0.6%.
Volume is down roughly 6% vs. the same time on Monday on the Nasdaq and 10% lower on the NYSE.
Gold gained 0.2% to $1,207 per troy ounce while U.S. crude oil futures added 0.2% to $72.21. Silver futures jumped 1.5% to $14.55 per ounce.
Apple ( AAPL ) added 0.5% to 221.95, maintaining a solid gain of 14% since it cleared a base-on-base buy point of 194.30. That base on base comprised of a seven-week double bottom that formed from March 13 to May 3, and a six-week flat base that began taking shape on June 7.
FANG stock Netflix ( NFLX ) continued to carve out the right side of a new base . Shares traded quietly, off less than 1 point at 368.65. The stock remains on the north side of its 50-day moving average, a bullish sign. Yet shares remain nearly 13% below the base's left-side peak of 423.20.
Square Remains A Market Leader Square ( SQ ), a leader in payment and transaction technology for small and midsize businesses, vaulted more than 11% and hit new highs in volume that ran more than 140% above typical levels. The big gains in heavy turnover implied that institutional demand remains fierce. The rally also stretched the stock's gain from a 52.60 correct buy point in a narrow seven-week double bottom to 81%.
That breakout took place in the week ended May 11, when Square bolted 11% higher for the week. The RS line, which gauges a stock's performance vs. the S&P 500, shot into new high ground.
The Jack Dorsey-led company also has expanded its gain from a breakout last year from a six-week flat base at 15.59 to more than 500%.
Notice on a weekly chart how the stock has found institutional buying support at or near the 10-week moving average three times since late June. A strong sell-off that takes shares sharply below the 10-week line, drawn in red in all IBD charts and in MarketSmith , would indicate that a significant correction may be underway.
Big Fundamentals Underpin The Technical Strength In Square Square's earnings per share have jumped 250%, 600%, 60%, 20% and 86% vs. year-ago levels in the past five quarters. Revenue climbed 26%, 33%, 36%, 45% and 48% over the same time frame.
Wall Street expects robust growth to continue. This year, analysts forecast full-year earnings to rise 67% to 45 cents a share, then go up an additional 76% to 79 cents in 2019.
The Street on consensus sees profit rising 57% to 11 cents a share in the third quarter of this year and up 88% to 15 cents in Q4.
Keep in mind that in Square's quarterly letter to shareholders, management reports two sets of top-line numbers: total net revenue and adjusted revenue, a much smaller number. Square defines adjusted revenue as total net revenue less transaction-based costs.
Analysts expect Square's third-quarter adjusted revenue to come in at $413.4 million, up 61% from the $257 million reported a year ago. Total net revenue back then was $585 million. Q4 adjusted revenue is seen at $438.8 million, up 55% vs. $283 million in the year-ago period. Square posted total net revenue of $616 million in Q4 of 2017.
Spinal surgical gear firm Globus Medical ( GMED ), featured in the new column IBD 50 Growth Stocks To Watch , rallied 1.5% to 54.88 in heavy trading. The stock is forming a saucer base and sits less than 5% below a potential buy point at 57.65.
Restaurants Rally Elsewhere, investors warmed up to restaurant stocks on news that burger and shake chain Sonic ( SONC ) is getting acquired by private equity firm Inspire Brands in a $2.3 billion cash and debt deal. Inspire owns the Arby's and Buffalo Wild Wings restaurant chains. Sonic boomed 18% higher to 43.37.
Shake Shack ( SHAK ) zoomed up 4.4% to 61.22, retaking its 50-day moving average for the first time since late July. The popular New York-based burger and fries fast casual chain is working on a new base. A breakout attempt on July 20 failed after Shake Shack formed a faulty cup that was less than four weeks long.
A good cup base should form over a minimum six weeks, and a cup with handle must be a minimum seven weeks in length.
Dow Jones industrial average component McDonald's ( MCD ) gained more than 2% to 167 in active turnover. The world's largest fast food chain is now firmly back above the key 50- and 200-day moving averages. The stock is still in basing mode, though.
The Street sees the burger and french fries veteran growing earnings 14% to $2 a share in the third quarter. McDonald's recently announced a hike in its quarterly cash payout by 15% to $1.16 a share. That bumps up the annualized dividend yield to nearly 2.8%, well above the 1.75% yield for the S&P 500.
